note: Candidates from the 2026-08-15 Potsdam verification pass. Four trees, pot_001 to pot_004, were delivered and published in data/cities/potsdam.json on 2026-08-15: two Naturdenkmal limes and two oaks in the Glienicke parkland on the Berlin bank of the bridge. A fifth and sixth tree, pot_005 (Door Oak of Pfaueninsel, register 6-101/B) and pot_006 (Schlosswiese Oak of Pfaueninsel, register 6-102/B), shipped the same pass and were retired 2026-08-16 per REVIEW.md's 2026-08-16 BLOCKER: both duplicate trees already published in data/cities/berlin.json (ber_012 and ber_011 respectively, same register ids, coordinates within 12-15m, same sources), and Potsdam's own FAQ already conceded they were 'not actually in Potsdam'. Their old URLs now redirect to the Berlin pages via RENAMED_TREE_SLUGS in site/src/lib/redirect-map.ts. Folded into blocked below so a future pass does not re-research them into Potsdam.

leads.name: The plane trees behind Jagdschloss Glienicke (Ahornblättrige Platane x3)
leads.place: Garten Klein-Glienicke, hinter dem Jagdschloss, Königstraße 36B
leads.reason: LEAD, access uncertain, not blocked outright. Three co-located London Planes (near-identical siting, treat as one collectible point if pursued, per the register-twin rule) stand in the walled garden directly behind Jagdschloss Glienicke, which has housed the Sozialpädagogisches Fortbildungsinstitut Berlin-Brandenburg (SFBB), a training institute, since 2007. Search results say the wider park around the building is open to the public 'at any time', but nothing found this pass confirms the specific fenced garden behind the building itself, as distinct from the surrounding open parkland (which is where pot_001 stands, and is NOT this garden). Per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md, when access cannot be stated honestly the tree waits as a lead rather than shipping or being blocked outright. A future pass should check the SFBB's own site or call to confirm whether the garden is open to casual visitors or only to institute guests; also present but unexamined at the same address, a Blutbuche (copper beech), register id 6-39/B, not yet a candidate. CONFIRMED 2026-08-15: this trio is genuinely distinct from the Pfaueninsel candidates verified the same pass (different coordinates, ~2km apart, different island entirely), not a re-surfacing of the same trees.

leads.name: Split-leaved oak near Schloss Pfaueninsel (Geschlitzblaettrige Trauben-Eiche)
leads.reason: Already published, under Berlin not Potsdam: this is the exact same tree as Berlin's ber_015 ("The Cut-Leaf Oak of Pfaueninsel"), same register id 6-108/B, same coordinates (52.431763, 13.121202 here vs 52.431763, 13.121202 there). Pfaueninsel is administratively part of Berlin (Steglitz-Zehlendorf), not Potsdam, even though it sits geographically closer to Potsdam and a distance-based register query pulls it into this city's candidate list. Same situation as the other two Pfaueninsel oaks this file already recorded as folded into ber_011 and ber_012. Marked 'duplicate' 2026-08-23 after leads.py's READY check surfaced this as needing a story, which it does not.

Also flag for a future pass: check whether 'westlich des Wirtshauses' places this tree in the inn's beer garden/private terrace rather than open parkland, which would be an access question under hard rule 10, not yet resolved.
